question: What is the primary purpose of excipients in a drug dosage form?

options.A: To combine with the active drug for delivery
options.B: To act as the active pharmaceutical ingredient
options.C: To neutralize the systemic toxicity of the drug
options.D: To accelerate hepatic metabolism of the medicine

explanation: Excipients are non-medicinal substances formulated alongside the active ingredient to aid in the delivery, stability, and absorption of the medication. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why must an intravenous injection be strictly free of particulate matter?

options.A: To prevent vascular occlusion and embolism
options.B: To ensure the medicine dissolves faster in the blood
options.C: To stop the immune system from destroying the drug
options.D: To allow the drug to bind more easily to plasma proteins

explanation: Particles introduced directly into the bloodstream can block small blood vessels, leading to dangerous embolisms and localized tissue ischemia. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which type of oral solid medication must NEVER be crushed before administration?
explanation: Enteric coatings protect the stomach lining from irritation or protect the drug from stomach acid; crushing them ruins this specialized delivery barrier. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the major pharmacological advantage of administering a drug via the sublingual route?

options.A: It guarantees a longer duration of drug action
options.C: It allows for safe administration to unconscious patients
options.D: It eliminates the risk of systemic side effects

explanation: Sublingual absorption allows the drug to enter the systemic circulation directly through oral mucosal blood vessels, avoiding breakdown by liver enzymes. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the essential procedural step immediately prior to pouring a dose of a liquid drug suspension?

options.A: Warming the bottle in warm water
options.B: Diluting the mixture with sterile water

explanation: Suspensions settle out of the liquid over time, so shaking ensures the active ingredient is evenly distributed throughout the dose poured. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why is it unsafe to use standard kitchen teaspoons when administering liquid oral medications at home?

options.A: Kitchen spoons dissolve sugary syrups upon direct contact
options.B: Kitchen spoons increase the risk of accidental microbial contamination
options.C: Kitchen spoons vary widely in volume and lack precise calibration
options.D: Kitchen spoons are usually made of reactive metal alloys

explanation: Household spoons are not standardized measurement tools, which frequently leads to underdosing or dangerous overdosing of liquid medications. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which topical formulation is characterized by an oil-heavy base that creates an occlusive moisture barrier?
explanation: Ointments have a high oil-to-water ratio, making them greasy and highly effective at locking moisture into dry skin. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h4)

question: Why is rotating the application site essential when managing a patient on continuous transdermal patch therapy?

options.A: To stop the adhesive backing from losing its stickiness
options.B: To accelerate the systemic absorption of the active drug
options.C: To ensure the old drug remnants are completely absorbed
options.D: To prevent localized skin irritation and breakdown

explanation: Applying transdermal patches to the exact same spot repeatedly causes contact dermatitis, skin breakdown, and altered drug absorption. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary clinical benefit of using a spacer with a metered-dose inhaler?

options.A: It decreases the total dose required for systemic effect
options.B: It improves lung deposition and reduces local oral deposition
options.C: It converts liquid medication into a dry powder format
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for patient breath-holding

explanation: Spacers slow down the aerosol cloud, allowing more time for the patient to inhale and reducing the amount of drug that sticks to the mouth and throat. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why must a patient rinse their mouth thoroughly with water after inhaling a corticosteroid medication?

options.A: To prevent the development of oral candidiasis or fungal infection
options.B: To stop the bitter chemical taste from causing nausea and vomiting
options.C: To prevent dental caries caused by the high sugar content in propellants
options.D: To enhance the systemic absorption of the swallowed drug residue

explanation: Corticosteroids suppress local immune responses in the oral cavity, predisposing patients to fungal overgrowth like thrush if the mouth is not cleared. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h5)

question: What is the most appropriate nursing action when an ordered medication dose appears unusual or unsafe for a patient?

options.A: Administer half the prescribed dose to maintain safety
options.B: Consult another nurse and administer the medication anyway
options.C: Clarify the order directly with the prescribing clinician
options.D: Omit the dose entirely and document patient refusal

explanation: Nurses act as a vital safety barrier; questioning ambiguous or potentially harmful orders with the prescriber prevents medication errors. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which of the following actions best demonstrates adherence to safe medication administration practices?

options.A: Documenting medication administration prior to patient consumption
options.B: Relying solely on memory when calculating complex pediatric doses
options.C: Leaving oral medications at the bedside for independent ingestion
options.D: Checking patient identity using at least two unique identifiers

explanation: Using identifiers such as name and hospital number ensures the right medication reaches the correct patient, avoiding wrong-patient errors. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h6)
